title: sdks: unify auth/retries and streaming parity across python/ts/go, ergonomics, v1.99.0
author: Marina Ortega
description:
Motivation: SDK consumers have inconsistent behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go for auth, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics which causes user confusion and production edge cases. This PR unifies the behavior and surface area across all three SDKs, improves ergonomics for streaming APIs (consistent callback/async/iterator patterns), fixes parity gaps discovered in recent compatibility tests, and bumps SDK versions to v1.99.0.

What changed: consolidated auth token refresh and retry hooks into a shared contract across SDKs; made retry/backoff policy configurable and consistent; added explicit streaming iterator helpers (Python async iterator, TS AsyncIterable, Go channel iterator); improved type definitions and docstrings; updated examples and tests; bumped package versions and CHANGELOG entries.

Implementation notes: shared semantics implemented separately in each language SDK rather than introducing a cross-language binary. Each SDK follows the same interface contract: `AuthProvider` with `get_token()`/`refresh()` hooks, `RetryPolicy` with `should_retry(response, error, attempt)` and a configurable max_attempts/backoff_strategy. Streaming helpers standardize chunk and error propagation and add an `on_chunk` ergonomic callback.

Migration notes: existing consumers with custom auth/retry should migrate to the new AuthProvider/RetryPolicy APIs. For simple use-cases the default implementations are backward-compatible; see migration examples in python/UPGRADING.md and typescript/UPGRADING.md.

Checklist:
- [x] Python: unified auth + retry, added AsyncStream iterator, updated docs and tests
- [x] TypeScript: unified auth + retry, AsyncIterable streaming helper, improved type defs
- [x] Go: auth interface, retry middleware, streaming helper channel pattern
- [x] E2E compatibility tests updated
- [x] CHANGELOG and version bumps

Related: ENG-8321 (auth reliability), ENG-8399 (streaming parity initiative), PM-412 (SDK ergonomics initiative).
